claim: The type-first full-support Q_N for stationary binary renewal blocks has pointwise likelihood ratio P_N(x)/Q_N(x) <= K_N N with log K_N=O(sqrt(N)) uniformly over all finite-mean gap laws.
inputs_and_proof: One stationary raw path; unknown arbitrary positive-integer gap law with finite but unbounded mean. Exact proof in outputs/research/root_renewal_prediction/PROOF.txt and outputs/research/acquisition_learning/cycle4/renewal_integer_code/RESULT.txt.
cost: Prefix marginals are exact; shared HJW suffix evaluation has O(n^3) coefficient/summand updates and polynomial exact bit complexity.
baseline_and_failure: HJW finite-block NML is same-interface statistical benchmark but efficient renewal marginalization is left unclear. Q_N is horizon-specific and not projectively consistent; all suffixes must use the same Q_N.
novelty: UNKNOWN; no firstness or priority claim.

claim: For one stationary finite-mean binary renewal path of length n, the exact suffix-average predictor has source-expected terminal conditional-KL risk O(n^{-1/2}); HJW Theorem 4 reports matching minimax order Theta(n^{-1/2}).
inputs_and_proof: Raw path only; no reset, support cutoff, mean bound, teacher, hidden state, or conditional query. Internal upper proof in renewal_integer_code/RESULT.txt; source-reported lower in HJW 2024.
cost: Exact fixed-horizon prefix marginals and all suffix ratios are polynomial bit-time; no memory or information advantage over an equally informed full-path predictor is claimed.
baseline_and_failure: CTW gives a log-factor upper control after HJW suffix conversion; expected terminal loss is distinct from fresh-history, worst-context, high-probability, cumulative, or multi-step risk.

claim: For fixed known q observed event marks with arbitrary joint next-gap/next-mark kernel and finite stationary mean, a row-urn colored-pool code stops on empty current row, allows unused other-row pools, and yields exact prefix marginals by a DP over span and row totals.
inputs_and_proof: One stationary path over {0,...,q}; marks/events are visible; no hidden mark compiler is claimed. Full Sol proof plus lead/Luna audit in sol_marked_renewal/RESULT.txt and marked_renewal_extension/RESULT.txt.
cost: Block regret <= log(q K_N N); fixed-q terminal bound is explicit; compiler is O_q(n^{q+6} log^2 n) conservative bit time and is not polynomial jointly in q,n.
baseline_and_failure: Binary q=1 subclass; all-zero option and the strict g>b tail are required. No hidden event marks, arbitrary HMM emissions, source reconstruction, or uniform-q runtime.

claim: At every current prefix length t, rerunning the t-specific fixed-horizon Q_{t+1} suffix-average predictor gives same-path terminal expected-KL risk at most [pi*sqrt(2t/3)+2*log(t+1)+log(2)+log(t+2)]/t <= 8/sqrt(t), without a declared terminal horizon; multiplying these outputs gives a projective sequential law with expected cumulative KL <= log(2)+16*sqrt(T).
inputs_and_proof: One raw stationary binary renewal path; arbitrary finite mean; full prefix retained. Proof in outputs/research/acquisition_learning/cycle4/renewal_anytime/RESULT.txt.
cost: O(t^3) coefficient updates per prefix, conservative O(t^9 log^2(t+2)) bit time; O(T^4) coefficient updates through T. It is not a compact-state or sublinear-memory algorithm.
baseline_and_failure: A new projective sequential law is formed by product of causal outputs. The fixed block family Q_N itself remains nonprojective; a checked witness is Q_2(X_1=1)=1/2 versus Q_3(X_1=1)=17/30. No pointwise likelihood-ratio or compact-memory claim.
novelty: UNKNOWN; bounded anytime prior-art search and external review not performed.

claim: Replacing each nonzero-suffix marginal's denominator products by exact (N!)^2 integer sums preserves the audited fixed-horizon predictor and reduces transient integer widths on dense active histories; at n=120 alternating input, median runtime was 3.41x faster and the largest transient integer was 7.5x narrower.
inputs_and_proof: Same one raw stationary binary renewal path and same Q_N. Exact divisibility proof and implementation in outputs/research/acquisition_learning/cycle4/renewal_integer_code/nfactorial/RESULT.txt and work/programmes/acquisition_learning/cycle4/renewal_integer_code/nfactorial/predictor.py.
cost: O(n^3) updates remain; at n=120 output components remain 20,519 bits and traced memory improves only 2.8%. The all-zero branch remains Fraction-based and showed no gain. Three-run measurements and exact operation ledger are in benchmark.json.
baseline_and_failure: Compared against the unchanged audited Fraction implementation on identical histories and direct prefix formulas. This is a constant-factor implementation measurement on a narrow input family, not an asymptotic improvement or statistical gain.

claim: For every n>=40000 and every possibly randomized predictor using the full n-bit path, some stationary finite-support renewal law has probability at least 1/160 of same-path terminal conditional KL risk at least (ln(2)-1/2)/(18 sqrt(n)); for each fixed delta<1/160 the minimax confidence quantile is Theta_delta(n^-1/2).
inputs_and_proof: Single stationary binary raw path; arbitrary finite mean; the lower-bound support varies with n. The proof retains both stationary censoring factors and invokes the posterior-ambiguity construction reconstructed in renewal_terminal_tail/RESULT.txt.
cost: Information-theoretic, applies to unlimited-computation full-history predictors. The type-first upper predictor has fixed-n tail at most min(1,B_n/epsilon) by Markov. Exact posterior checker passes four small exhaustive instances; it is finite diagnostics, not the all-n proof.
baseline_and_failure: The lower bound is against the strongest same-data full-path baseline. It concerns conditional KL before the next outcome, not independent-history risk, realized one-step score, or a time-uniform event for one fixed source.
novelty: UNKNOWN; this strengthens the source's expected-risk Bayes construction but no priority claim is made.

claim: For q=2 hidden event marks with only binary event times observed, the candidate projected uniform row-urn code's integer-scaled prefix/full-block mass is #P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions for explicit horizons N bounded by the raw trajectory length. An exact polynomial-time compiler for all fixed-Q_N conditionals would therefore imply FP=#P.
inputs_and_proof: The code and q=2 are supplied; no source parameters, hidden marks, transition oracle, or growing q are supplied. Full reduction in outputs/research/sol_hidden_renewal/RESULT.txt uses fresh-gap padding/interpolation, a Hadamard tensor transform, Eulerian medial words and pinned partition extraction. Independent internal Luna audit in outputs/research/acquisition_learning/cycle4/hidden_renewal_audit/RESULT.txt found no fatal gap; it scopes #P membership to unary or explicitly polynomially bounded N. The hardness queries use explicit raw paths with N=|x|.
cost: Reduction uses O(m) exact code queries, each with explicit horizon N=O(|G|^2); all integer/rational quantities have polynomial bit length. Scaled prefix mass membership in #P is stated for unary N or N bounded by explicit path size. An exact exp(O(q sqrt(N))) count-vector fallback and polynomial leaves for bounded distinct observed gaps are described by Sol.
baseline_and_failure: The result is for exact evaluation of this projected code's prefixes/full blocks, not hardness of its suffix-averaged terminal predictor, not a lower bound for every optimal predictor, and not an FPRAS/improper approximation barrier. Interpolation is cancellation-heavy, so it is not an approximation-preserving reduction.
novelty: UNKNOWN; focused independent internal audit found no fatal gap, but external validation and priority search remain pending.

claim: For every fixed q>=2, the exact projected uniform q-state row-urn code likelihood on an explicit full-span binary block with each positive gap value occurring at most twice has a polynomial-bit FPRAS in N, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1).
inputs_and_proof: One explicit N-bit binary block; q is fixed and known as part of the theorem family. No hidden states, pool, source parameter, code oracle or succinct horizon is supplied. Proof and independent reconstruction in fixed_q_pair_bond_fpras/RESULT.txt and AUDIT.txt.
cost: Correction mean is at least (3/4)128^(-2(q-1))(m+1)^(-5(q-1)). A coarse JS-derived arithmetic bound for the correction phase is O_q(m^(15(q-1)+16) epsilon^-4 log(delta^-1) polylog(m/epsilon,delta^-1)); finite-bit rational simulation is internally reconstructed, not executable or benchmarked.
baseline_and_failure: No result for growing q, multiplicity >=3, censored prefixes, suffix prediction, generic hidden-renewal reconstruction, AP-hardness, or approximation hardness. This is a restricted likelihood computation, not a teacher-free learner.
novelty: UNKNOWN; no firstness, priority, or external proof-validation claim.
